title: The selection of single-domain antibody fragments \(iDAbs) by intracellular antibody capture in yeast
protocol: Weigh 100 g of D-glucose and add 500 ml of Milli-Q water.
Filter the glucose solution through a 0.2 μm filter.
Store the filtered glucose solution at 4°C for up to 3 months.
Weigh 2 g of L-adenine and add 500 ml of Milli-Q water.
Filter the adenine solution through a 0.2 μm filter.
Store the filtered adenine solution at 4°C for up to 3 months.
Dissolve 10 g of yeast extract and 20 g of peptone in 900 ml of Milli-Q H2O.
Autoclave the mixture at 0.5 bar and 121 °C for 20 min.
Cool the autoclaved solution to 55°C.
Add 100 ml of filtered 20% glucose solution (w/v) and 10 ml of 100x adenine solution to the cooled mixture.
Pour ~25 ml into sterile 9 cm dishes for plates.
Store YPAD medium and plates at RT for up to 1 month.
Dissolve 2.4 g of yeast nitrogen base, 10 g of ammonium sulphate, 20 g of succinic acid, 0.1 g of tyrosine, and 12 g of NaOH in 400 ml of Milli-Q H2O.
Adjust the pH to 7.0 by adding more NaOH pellets as needed.
Autoclave the mixture at 0.5 bar and 121 °C for 20 min.
Store 5× Yeast complete medium without amino acids (5× YC w/o AA) at RT for up to 1 month.
Dissolve 1 g of phenylalanine, 1 g of isoleucine, 2 g of arginine, 1 g of valine, 1 g of aspartic acid, 1 g of proline, 1 g of serine and 2 g of threonine in 200 ml of Milli-Q H2O.
Filter sterilize the amino acid mixture.
Prepare 10 ml aliquots in 15 ml Falcon tubes.
Store amino acid supplements mix minus 7 dropout (AA mix-7) at 4°C for up to 6 months.
Dissolve 2 g of tryptophan in 200 ml of Milli-Q H2O and filter sterilize.
Prepare 10 ml aliquots of amino acid stocks and store at 4°C for up to 6 months.
Dissolve 2 g of lysine in 200 ml of Milli-Q H2O and filter sterilize.
Dissolve 1 g of methionine in 200 ml of Milli-Q H2O and filter sterilize.
Dissolve 2 g of adenine in 200 ml of Milli-Q H2O and filter sterilize.
Dissolve 1 g of histidine in 200 ml of Milli-Q H2O and filter sterilize.
Dissolve 2 g of leucine in 200 ml of Milli-Q H2O and filter sterilize.
Dissolve 1 g of uracil in 1 liter of Milli-Q H2O and filter sterilize.
Store Ura stock at 4°C for up to 6 months.
Dissolve 168.2 g of 3-AT in 1 l of Milli-Q H2O and filter sterilize.
Store 2 M 3-AT stock at -20°C for up to 6 months.
Mix 20 ml of 5× YC w/o AA with 10 ml of filtered 20% (w/v) glucose solution.
Add 1 ml of AA mix–7 and 1 ml of each amino acid supplement (except uracil).
Add 10 ml of 10× uracil solution.
Autoclave Milli-Q H2O to a final volume of 100 ml.
Store the YC dropout medium at room temperature for up to 1 month.
Add 20 g of agar to 200 ml of 5× YC w/o AA in a 1 liter bottle with a magnetic stirrer.
Autoclave the mixture at 0.5 bar and 121 °C for 20 min.
Cool the autoclaved mixture to 60 °C in a water bath.
Combine 100 ml of filtered 20% (w/v) glucose solution, 10 ml of AA mix-7, and 10 ml of each amino acid supplement.
Add 100 ml of 10× uracil solution to the mixture.
If needed, add 3-AT stock at this point.
Make up to 1 liter by adding pre-warmed (55 °C) autoclaved Milli-Q H2O.
Pour the mixture immediately into sterile dishes in a sterile hood.
Leave plates overnight at room temperature to solidify and dry.
Replace the lid, invert the plate, and store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Check for contaminating colonies before using stored plates.
Dissolve 1 g of salmon sperm DNA in 50 ml of 1× TE using a magnetic stirrer at 4°C until completely dissolved.
Sonicate the salmon sperm DNA on ice for 30 seconds with a large sonicator probe using 20-30% power to reduce viscosity.
Prepare 1 ml aliquots in 1.5 ml microtubes and store at -20°C indefinitely.
Boil the salmon sperm DNA for 10 minutes before use.
Weigh 50 g of PEG3350, add 100 ml Milli-Q H2O, and pass through a 0.2 μm filter.
Store the 50% PEG solution at room temperature for up to one month.
Weigh 25.5 g of LiAc, add 200 ml of Milli-Q H2O, adjust pH to 7.5 with glacial acetic acid, and adjust final volume to 250 ml.
Autoclave the 1 M LiAc solution at 0.5 bar and 121°C for 20 minutes.
Store the autoclaved 1 M LiAc solution at room temperature for up to three months.
Mix 10 ml of 1M LiAc, 10 ml of 10× TE, and 80 ml of autoclaved Milli-Q H2O to prepare a fresh TE-PEG solution each time of use.
Mix 10 ml of 1 M LiAc, 10 ml of 10×TE, and 80 ml of 50% PEG (w/v) to prepare a fresh LiAc–TE–PEG solution each time of use.
Dissolve 10KU of lyticase in 1 ml Milli-Q H2O to make a working stock of 10U/μl.
Weigh 40.8 g of sodium acetate 3H2O, add Milli-Q H2O to 90 ml.
Adjust the solution to pH 5.2 with glacial acetic acid and add Milli-Q H2O to a final volume of 100 ml.
Autoclave the 3 M sodium acetate solution at 0.5 bar and 121 °C for 20 min.
Store the autoclaved 3 M sodium acetate solution at RT for up to 6 months.
Dissolve 16 g of tryptone, 10 g of yeast extract, and 5 g of NaCl in 1 liter of Milli-Q H2O.
Autoclave the 2× TY medium at 0.5 bar and 121 °C for 20 min.
Store the autoclaved 2× TY medium at RT for up to 3 months if no contamination becomes apparent.
Weigh 15 g of bacto-agar, 10 g of tryptone, 5 g of yeast extract, and 8 g of NaCl, add Milli-Q H2O to 1 liter.
Autoclave the mixture at 0.5 bar and 121 °C for 20 min.
Allow the autoclaved mixture to cool to 55 °C.
Add antibiotics (ampicillin or chloramphenicol) while stirring and pour into sterile dishes.
Store the TYE plates at 4 °C for up to 3 months.
Dissolve 4 g of tryptone, 1 g of yeast extract, and 0.1 g of NaCl in 150 ml of Milli-Q H2O.
Add 0.5 ml of 1 M KCl to the solution.
Adjust the pH to 7 with NaOH.
Bring the volume up to 194.4 ml.
Autoclave at 0.5 bar and 121 °C for 20 min.
Add 2 ml of 1 M filter-sterilized MgCl2 to the cooled solution.
Add 3.6 ml of filter-sterilized 20% (w/v) glucose to reach a final volume of 200 ml.
Store the SOC medium at room temperature for up to 3 months.
Make stocks of antibiotics as 1,000× solutions and store in aliquots at -20 °C for up to 6 months.
Prepare ampicillin stock solution at 100 mg/ml in dH2O.
Prepare chloramphenicol stock solution at 15 mg/ml in absolute ethanol.
Clone the antigen (bait) cDNA as an in-frame fusion with LexA DNA-binding domain in pBTM116 vector using standard genetic cloning methods.
Streak L40 yeast from glycerol stock onto YPAD agar plate and leave to grow for 2-3 days at 30 °C.
Inoculate a single colony into 2 ml of YPAD medium the day before yeast transformation and incubate overnight with shaking at 30 °C.
Measure the OD600 of the overnight culture.
Calculate the volume required to dilute the culture to an OD600 between 0.15-0.2 in 10 ml of YPAD medium.
Dilute the overnight culture 1:10 before measuring the OD600 for an accurate reading.
Culture the yeast at 30°C with shaking (~225 rpm) until the OD600 reaches 0.4-0.5.
Pellet the yeast culture by centrifugation for 5 minutes, 1,000g at 4°C.
Remove the medium and resuspend the pellet in 10 ml of sterile Milli-Q H2O.
Centrifuge again for 5 minutes, 1,000g at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the final yeast pellet in 100 μl of freshly made, sterile TE-LiAc.
Denature the salmon sperm DNA by incubating at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Chill the denatured salmon sperm DNA on ice immediately for at least 2 minutes.
Mix 200 ng of bait plasmid and 100 μg of denatured salmon sperm carrier DNA in a sterile 1.5 ml microtube.
Add the DNA mixture to 100 μl of competent yeast and mix by flicking the tube.
Add 600 μl of freshly prepared sterile PEG-LiAc-TE solution and mix inverting the tube several times.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 30°C with shaking at 225 rpm.
Add 70 μl of DMSO and mix gently by inversion.
Heat shock for 15 minutes in a 42°C water bath.
Place on ice for 2 minutes.
Fill the microtube with sterile Milli-Q H2O.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation for 5 minutes at 3,000g at RT.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μl of sterile 1xTE.
Plate 50 μl of the transformed yeast onto a 10 cm YC-W plate.
Incubate the plate for 2-3 days at 30 °C.
Pick a single yeast colony from the YC-W plate and transfer it into 5 ml of YC-W media in a 50 ml falcon tube.
Resuspend by vortexing.
Streak a small amount onto YC-W plate for short-term storage and incubate for 2-3 days at 30 °C.
Take 500 μl of the overnight culture for protein analysis.
Freeze the remaining culture by adding an equal volume of 30% sterile glycerol solution.
Centrifuge 500 μl of yeast culture for 1 minute at 3,000g.
Remove the supernatant and wash the pellet in 500 μl Milli-Q H2O.
Centrifuge again for 1 minute at 3,000g.
Resuspend the pellet in 300 μl of Milli-Q H2O and mix with an equal volume of 0.6M NaOH.
Incubate cells at RT for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the cells for 1 minute at 3,000g.
Carefully remove the supernatant and resuspend in 20 μl of 5% SDS.
Add 20 μl 2x SDS-PAGE buffer to the sample.
Boil the sample for 5 minutes.
Load 20 μl of the supernatant for western blot analysis.
Detect the fusion bait protein using anti-LexA antibody.
Streak a single colony from the established bait line onto a new YC-W plate and incubate at 30 °C for 2-3 days.
Pick a single colony into 100 μl of sterile 1xTE and resuspend with a pipette.
Use sterile inoculating loops to re-streak the yeast onto a series of YC-WH plates containing various concentrations of 3-AT (ranging from 0-50 mM).
Incubate for 2-3 days at 30°C.
Assess yeast growth to determine the minimal concentration of 3-AT that prevents self-activation.
Inoculate 5-10 colonies of the established bait strain in 1 ml of autoclaved Milli-Q H2O in a sterile 15 ml falcon tube and resuspend by vortexing.
Inoculate the yeast suspension into 200 ml of YC-W media in a 500 ml Erlenmeyer flask.
Culture overnight at 30°C with shaking at 225 rpm.
Measure the OD600 of the overnight culture and calculate the volume required to dilute this culture to an OD600 between 0.15-0.2 in 1 L of YPAD medium.
Take the calculated volume from step 40 and dispense into a 225 ml Falcon conical tube.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 1000g at RT and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the yeast pellet in 5 ml YPAD medium and inoculate into 1 L of pre-warmed YPAD medium in a 2.5 Erlenmeyer flask.
Incubate at 30°C with shaking at 225 rpm until the OD600 reaches between 0.4-0.5, usually taking 3-4 hours.
Transfer the yeast culture into 5x 225 ml conical tubes and pellet the cells by centrifugation for 5 minutes at 1000g at 4°C.
Resuspend each pellet in 40 ml of sterile Milli-Q H2O and combine into one 225 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the yeast cells for 5 minutes at 1000g at 4°C.
Resuspend the yeast pellet again in 200 ml of sterile Milli-Q H2O and centrifuge the yeast cells for 7 minutes at 1000g at 4°C.
Resuspend the yeast pellet in 8 ml of freshly prepared TE-LiAc.
Keep the resuspended yeast at 4°C until use (no more than 1 hour on ice).
Denature the salmon sperm DNA by incubating at 95°C for 5 minutes and chilling immediately on ice for at least 2 minutes.
Combine 300 μg of a yeast single domain library DNA with 10 mg of denatured salmon sperm DNA and mix well by pipetting.
Add this DNA mixture to 8 ml of competent yeast cells (from step 52) and mix well by inversion.
Transfer the DNA-competent yeast mix into a 250 ml Erlenmeyer flask and add 60 ml of freshly prepared, sterile PEG-TE-LiAc solution, mixing by swirling.
Incubate for 30 minutes at 30 °C with shaking at 225 rpm.
Add 7 ml of DMSO and mix gently by swirling (do not vortex).
Heat shock the mixture for 15 minutes at 42°C in a water bath and swirl to mix every 2 minutes.
Place the sample on ice for 2 minutes and transfer it into a 225 ml conical tube.
Fill the tube with sterile Milli-Q H2O and centrifuge for 5 minutes at 2,500g at room temperature.
Carefully decant the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, gently resuspend the pellet in 10 ml of sterile Milli-Q H2O, then fill the tube with 200 ml of sterile Milli-Q H2O.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 2,500g at room temperature and remove the supernatant by pipetting.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 ml of sterile 1xTE buffer.
Make 100 μl serial dilutions of transformed yeast from step 62 (equivalent to 10 μl (1:10), 1 μl (1:100), 0.1 μl (1:1,000), and 0.01 μl (1:10,000) in 1xTE).
Plate the diluted yeast onto 9 cm YC-WL plates.
Incubate for 2-3 days at 30 °C.

Count the number of yeast colonies and multiply this number by the dilution factor to determine the total number of transformants (e.g., 150 colonies counted on a YC-WL plate spreading equivalent to 0.1 μl (dilution 1:1000) of yeast is 150 x 1000 = 1.5 x 10^5 per 100 μl of transformed yeast plated out for colony counting).
Plate all of the transformed yeast from step 62 onto 5x Nunc bioassay dishes with YC-WLH agar.
Incubate for 4-5 days at 30 °C.
Pick yeast colonies that have grown to about 2-3 mm in diameter into 50 μl 1xTE separately.
Re-streak individual colonies onto a new 6 cm YC-WLH plate as the master plate.
Grow the master plates for 2-3 days at 30 °C.
Inoculate all positive yeast colonies from the master plates into 5 ml YC-L medium in a 15 ml Falcon tube.
Incubate overnight at 30 °C with shaking at 225 rpm.
Centrifuge culture at 1000g for 5 minutes.
Pour off supernatant and resuspend in 200 μl YC medium.
Add 20 μl of lyticase solution (10U/μl) to the yeast suspension and mix by vortexing.
Incubate at 37 °C for 30-60 minutes with shaking at 225 rpm.
Add 10 μl of 20% SDS to the mixture and vortex vigorously.
Put the sample through one freeze/thaw cycle (-20°C) and vortex again.
Bring the volume of the lysate to 200 μl in 1xTE buffer.
Add 200 μl of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) to the lysate.
Vortex vigorously for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge at 15,000g for 10 minutes at RT.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a fresh tube.
Add 20 μl of 3 M Sodium acetate and 500 μl of 100% ethanol to the aqueous phase.
Place the mixture at -70°C or in dry ice for 1 hour.
Centrifuge at 15,000g for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Dry the pellet for 10-15 minutes at room temperature.
Resuspend the pellet with 20 μl Milli-Q H2O.
Set up a 50 μl PCR reaction with primer pair A according to the manufacturer’s protocol for Phusion High-Fidelity DNA polymerase.
Run the PCR program: initial denaturation at 95°C for 2 min, followed by 30 cycles of 95°C for 20 s, 55°C for 10 s and 72°C for 20 s, with a final extension step at 72°C for 5 minutes.
Take 2 μl of each PCR reaction and run on a 1.5% agarose (w/v) gel to confirm the size of the PCR products.
Run the remaining PCR reaction on a 1.5% agarose (w/v) gel and excise the correct sized band.
Extract DNA from the gel pieces using QIAquick gel extraction kit.
Elute the final DNA volume in 30 μl in a 1.5 ml microfuge tube.
Set up 100 μl PCR reactions with 2 μl of 10 μM primers sFvVP16F and sFvVP16R.
Add 1 μl of each DNA product from primer pairs A and B for VH library or C and D for VL library to the PCR reaction.
Carry out the PCR assembly using the thermocycling conditions as specified in Step 90.
Take 2 μl of each PCR reaction and run on a 1.5% agarose gel.
Purify the remaining PCR reaction with a QIAspin PCR purification kit if the analytical gel shows correct size PCR products (669–708 bp for VH and 645 bp for VL).
Elute the purified DNA in 50 μl in a 1.5 ml micro tube.
Add 10 μl of 10× NEB Cutsmart buffer to the eluted PCR fragment.
Mix well with 2 μl (40 U) of SfiI restriction enzyme and incubate for at least 3 hrs at 50 °C.
Set up a digestion of 5 μg of pVP16* yeast plasmid, 5 μl of 10× NEB Cutsmart buffer, and 2.5 μl (50 U) of SfiI restriction enzyme in a 100 μl total reaction.
Mix well the components for the digestion of pVP16* yeast plasmid.
Incubate the mixture at 50 °C until completely digested (for at least 3 hrs).
Confirm complete digestion of the vector by electrophoresis of 2 μl (0.2 μg) of the digestion reaction on a 1–1.5% agarose gel compared with the uncut plasmid.
Add 1 μl of 10× cutsmart buffer to each SfiI digest.
Add 2.5 μl (50U) of NotI-HF enzyme to the SfiI digests and mix well.
Incubate the mixture for 3 hours at 37°C.
Confirm complete digestion of the pVP16* plasmid by electrophoresis of a 2 μl aliquot on a 1.5% agarose gel.
Add 1 μl of calf-intestine alkaline phosphatase (CIAP) to the SfiI-NotI digested pVP16* reaction.
Incubate with CIAP for an additional 30 minutes at 37°C.
Run the digested DNAs on a preparative 2% agarose gel (for PCR products) or 0.8% agarose gel (for CIAP-treated linearized pVP16* plasmid).
Cut the appropriate band from the gel containing the single-domain DNA fragment (around 333–396 bp) and linearized pVP16* (8.2 kbp).
Extract the DNA from the pieces of agarose gel using QIAquick gel extraction kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute the DNA with 30 μl of elution buffer.
Set up a set of 30 μl ligations in sterile microfuge tubes with 2 μg of purified SfiI-NotI linear pVP16* plasmid and 150 ng of purified SfiI-NotI PCR fragment (vector:insert ratio of ~1:3).
Add 1 μl of T4 DNA ligase to the ligation mixture.
Add 3 μl of 10× ligase buffer to the ligation mixture.
Incubate overnight at 15°C or on ice.
Store ligation samples at −20°C for up to 2 weeks after overnight reaction.
Add 59 μl of H2O, 1 μl of yeast tRNA (10 mg ml−1), and 10 μl of 3 M sodium acetate to the sample.
Mix well.
Add 250 μl of ice-cold absolute ethanol to the mixture, vortex, and incubate on dry ice or at −70°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge the sample for 10 min at 15,000g, room temperature (RT).
Remove supernatant and wash DNA pellet once with 500 μl of 70% ethanol, then centrifuge again at 15,000g, RT.
Remove ethanol from the pellet and dry for 10–15 min at RT.
Resuspend the DNA pellet in 10 μl of 1× TE buffer.
Use 1 μl of ligation reaction per 50 μl of NEB®5-alpha competent E. coli or follow electroporation instructions from the manufacturer for bacterial transformation.
After transformation, add SOC medium to a total volume of 1 ml and transfer to a sterile Falcon tube.
Culture transformed bacteria in SOC medium at 37°C with shaking (225 rpm) for 60 min.
Prepare tenfold serial dilutions (from 1:100 to 1:10,000) from the transformation mixture and plate on TYE + ampicillin plates (100 μg ml−1).
Incubate plates overnight at 37°C.
Inoculate 10–20 individual colonies from titration plates in 2 ml of 2× TY with 100 μg/ml ampicillin.
Culture overnight at 37°C with shaking (225 r.p.m.).
Harvest the bacteria and prepare plasmid DNA using QIAspin plasmid mini kits according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Digest 0.5 μg of each plasmid with SfiI at 50°C for at least 3 h.
Digest 0.5 μg of each plasmid with NotI at 37°C for at least 1 h.
Run the digestion products on a 1.5% agarose gel (w/v).
Sequence the plasmids that contain inserts of the correct size using sFvVP16F or sFvVP16R primers.
Multiply the transformation efficiency from step by the fraction of plasmids with insert determined from sequence data to calculate library size from 1 μl of ligation reaction in step 112.
Calculate volume of ligation required for a sub-library size of >1x10^6.
Repeat bacteria transformation with remaining ligation reaction from step.
Plate the transformation mix onto ten large square TYE plates (25 cm × 25 cm) containing 100 μg/ml ampicillin.
Incubate the plates overnight at 37°C.
Add 5 ml of 2× TY + 100 μg/ml ampicillin to each plate.
Scrape all bacterial colonies from each plate using a sterile spreader.
Transfer scraped bacteria suspension into 50 ml Falcon tubes.
Make bacterial pellets by spinning for 30 min at 2,500g, 4°C.
Extract the plasmid DNA from the recovered cells using a QIAGEN Plasmid Midi or Maxi Kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Measure the quality and concentration of the plasmid DNA by determining the UV spectrum from 220 and 300 nm.
Screen the CDR2 sub-library using the same bait line expressing LexA-antigen from step 36, following steps 37-65.
Plate all of the transformed yeast onto 5x large YC − WLH plates containing 25, 50, 75 or 100 mM 3-AT.
Incubate for 4–7 d at 30 °C.
Pick those yeast colonies that are 1–2 mm in size and separately streak onto a new 14- or 9-cm small round YC − WLH plate (as master plate).
Incubate the plates at 30 °C until yeast growth is visible (1–2 d).
Inoculate the yeast colonies from the YC−WLH plate into 5 ml of YC−L medium.
Extract plasmid DNA from yeast cultures.
Measure the quality and concentration of the extracted plasmid DNA by determining the UV spectrum from 220 to 300 nm.
Set up two 50 μl PCR reactions using plasmid DNA from step 132 (20-50 ng) with primer pairs A: sFvVP16F and rdmVHCDR1Rev, and B: VHCDR1Fw and sFvVP16R for VH libraries.
Set up two 50 μl PCR reactions using plasmid DNA from step 132 (20-50 ng) with primer pairs C: sFvVP16F and rdmVLCDR1Re, and D: VLCDR1Fw and sFvVP16R for VL libraries.
Carry out the PCR reaction as described in step 90.
Extract and purify the amplified PCR fragments as in steps 91-93.
Carry out PCR assembly and digest the assembled PCR fragment with SfiI and NotI as in steps 94–98.
Construct the third sub-library by cloning the PCR fragments from step 136 into SfiI and NotI sites of pVP16* DNA as described before in steps 99-125.
Repeat the protocol from steps 126-130 using the library constructed in step 137, but use YC − WLH plates containing a higher concentration of 3-AT than with the second round screening.
Inoculate yeast colonies from the YC − WLH plate into 5 ml of YC − L medium.
Culture yeast overnight at 30 °C with shaking (225 r.p.m).
Harvest yeast and extract plasmid DNA from yeast culture.
Transform 1–5 μl of the DNA stock into bacteria using electroporation or chemical transformation.
Plate transformed bacteria onto TYE + ampicillin plates.
Grow bacteria overnight at 37 °C.
Inoculate bacterial colonies into 2 ml of 2× TY containing 100 μg/ml ampicillin.
Extract plasmid DNA from bacteria using QIAprep Spin MiniPrep kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Digest 5 μl of DNA with SfiI and NotI enzymes (digest first with SfiI for 3 hrs at 50 °C, cool to 37 °C, add NotI and continue the digest for a further 3 h at 37 °C).
Separate digestion products on a 1.5% agarose gel.
Prepare competent L40 yeast as described in steps 2-9.
Denature salmon sperm DNA as in step 10.
Mix 200 ng of pBTM116 vector with 200 ng of isolated yeast single-domain VP16 plasmid DNAs and 100 μg of salmon sperm carrier DNA.
Add the DNA mixture into 100 μl of each competent yeast bait and mix well.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μl of sterile 1xTE.
Plate 50 μl of the transformed yeast onto a 10 cm YC-WL plate.
Incubate the plate for 2-3 days at 30 °C.
Spot 10 μl of each resuspended yeast onto one 10 cm YC−WL plate and one 10 cm YC−WLH plate.
Incubate at 30 °C for 1–3 d until yeast growth is visible.
